feed.title: Awesome Security & AI Research: a weekly vetted briefing
feed.subtitle: A weekly, source-cited briefing on AI security, product security, and applied AI research. Every finding is vetted, distilled to one lesson and one action, and filed by field. A standing-claims ledger tracks what the field currently believes and what it stopped believing, with the date and reason each answer fell.

entry.title: PHP releases fixes for 17 flaws, seven of them critical
entry.summary: October's PHP2Shell fixes do not cover these new remote code execution paths, so teams that already patched once still need to update.

entry.title: F5 patches five critical NGINX flaws as public exploit code appears
entry.summary: Upgrade NGINX to a fixed build now and do not count on ASLR or traffic volume to keep the HTTP/2 bugs out of reach.

entry.title: New unpatched PHP RCE (CVE-2026-115560) is separate from PHP2Shell
entry.summary: Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 on any PHP host that might switch session serializers at runtime. It is the stopgap for CVE-2026-115560 until a patch ships.

entry.title: Attackers exploit critical Cisco Expressway flaw to breach a Russian organization
entry.summary: A perimeter appliance with a public exploit can become a foothold into internal systems within weeks of the patch, so patch fast and segment the network.

entry.title: PHP patches seven critical remote code execution flaws
entry.summary: Session handling and PHP-FPM request parsing are now recurring sources of code execution, so patch PHP promptly after the PHP2Shell wave.

entry.title: Azure API Management flaw exposed secrets, tied to Norwegian energy firm incidents
entry.summary: If you run Azure API Management Classic, rotate every secret and named value stored in it and check access logs.

entry.title: Amazon: China-linked attackers used AI agents to exploit a university zero-day
entry.summary: Attacker agents now chain recon, failed attempts and a fresh zero-day over a day with little human input.

entry.title: OpenAI and Cisco launch Shirudo, agent-written eBPF shields for unpatched Linux
entry.summary: Virtual patching by agents is arriving; require operator approval, shadow-mode testing and signing before any machine-written kernel control runs in production.

entry.title: Signal blocks OS AI agents from screenshotting chats, calls fix incomplete
entry.summary: Apps cannot rely on a screenshot block to keep data from agents that hold broad OS permissions, so permission scope for agents needs its own controls.

entry.title: Dragos canary prompts found three AI hosting providers breached
entry.summary: Assume every router and host on the path can read and keep your prompt, so keep live credentials and private URLs out of prompts, whatever privacy flag is set.

entry.title: Wiz shows ARTEX and Cairn leak numeric intent IDs into victim logs
entry.summary: Agent harnesses leak their own bookkeeping into victim telemetry, giving defenders a cheap pacing and linking signal when paired with a tool-specific anchor.

entry.title: Harness choice alone can double an agent's cost
entry.summary: On the same model and task, the harness alone changed cost up to about 2x at similar accuracy, and coding agents' first call ranges from about 1.9k to 32k input tokens.

entry.title: Learn per-repo cost controls from past coding agent runs
entry.summary: A controller that learns from earlier runs in the same repository which tools to prune, which short notes to inject and when to stop unproductive failure loops cut coding-agent cost by 18-31% on SWE-Bench with comparable task success.

entry.title: Use one-hour cache markers when sessions pause over five minutes
entry.summary: Harnesses that write 5-minute prompt-cache markers re-buy their whole context after an idle gap longer than five minutes, while harnesses with 1-hour markers kept about 86% cache hits after a 390-second pause.

entry.title: Constrained decoding wins for structured output, not TOON
entry.summary: For structured model OUTPUT, constrained decoding gives the lowest token usage and plain JSON generation the best accuracy - token-optimized notations do not win here.
